result_text:
Folders whose names start with `mock` or `__mock` are now classified as mock resources (test code), at any depth and with either separator style. The full `codeanalyzer` suite passes (332 tests, 3 skipped, none failing) along with the two targeted classes.

**What changed**
- `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java`: the two folder rules (`.*/__mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*` and `.*/mock[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+/.*`) are replaced by one rule, `.*/(__)?mock[^/]*/.*`. The folder part accepts any characters except a path separator, so plain `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/` and `mock模拟/` all match. The old character class also covered `mock`-prefixed folders that the new rule still covers, so no previously matched folder is lost.
- `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsMockTest.java` (new): checks the new folder names and the existing ones (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`), Windows-style paths, and the non-matches (`remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`).

I left the existing `mockapi`, `[Mm]ocks` and `_mock.*` rules alone, since the change didn't need them touched. I did not commit.
